questions.q: According to this lesson, which five things should every piece of business process automation document?
options: Purpose, trigger/entry criteria, who it affects, dependencies, and owner/last-reviewed date
Object API name, record type, page layout, profile, and permission set
Creation date, file size, folder location, author's email, and version number
Flow type, element count, variable names, loop count, and debug log size
questions.explain: Those five questions let the next person understand what the automation does and why, without reverse-engineering it.

questions.q: Why is a document that nobody knows to look for not considered a real handoff?
options: Because it must be printed on paper to count
Because handoff requires a predictable location plus an actual walkthrough with the incoming owner
Because Salesforce deletes unused documents automatically
Because only Salesforce administrators are allowed to read documentation
questions.explain: A file that exists but isn't discoverable, with no one walking the new owner through it, functions the same as no documentation at all.

questions.q: In the example documentation entry for Lesson 11's quote approval, what does the 'Depends on' line list?
options: The sales team's quarterly quota
The company's annual revenue
The Discount_Percent__c field, the Manager lookup on User, and the Status picklist
A list of every user in the org
questions.explain: Dependencies capture the other fields and structures the automation relies on to function correctly.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue documentation matters even for automation that's working correctly today?
options: Working automation never actually needs maintenance
Salesforce requires documentation to pass validation
Documentation makes automation run faster
Because the person who understands it today may be gone in six months, and the next person still has to maintain or extend it
questions.explain: Chapter 2's maintenance topics -- collisions, recursion, upkeep -- all depend on someone being able to explain what automation is supposed to do.

questions.q: What is the difference between leaving comments inside a Flow and writing proper handoff documentation?
options: There is no difference -- they accomplish the same thing
Comments inside a Flow only help someone already looking at that specific Flow; documentation is meant to be found and walked through independently
Flow comments are always more detailed than written documentation
Handoff documentation cannot include any technical details
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes documentation that lives somewhere discoverable and is actively handed off from notes buried inside the build itself.
